newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: PerezCompanc wins Venezuela Acema oil deal.
newsitem.headline: PerezCompanc wins Venezuela Acema oil deal.

text.p: Argentine oil company Perez Companc, in association with Corporacion Corepli de Venezuela, agreed Monday to pay $41 million for the contract to operate Venezuela's Acema oil field, state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) said.
The consortium was among 12 bidders on the first day of Venezuela's third round of oil operating contract auctions. It narrowly won by only 22 dollars over the second highest bidder.

The field, discovered in 1954 in eastern Venezuela, currently produces 500 barrels per day (bpd) from four active wells and has proven reserves of 33 million barrels, according to PDVSA estimates. Thirty other wells are inactive.

Under the 20-year contract, the operator will produce hydrocarbons on behalf of PDVSA subsidiary Corpoven in exchange for a fee worked out on a sliding scale. The operator must also invest at least $5 million within three years, although PDVSA expects investment to be higher.
The field was the last of five reserved for consortia with at least 30 percent Venezuelan participation.
Contracts for four other fields already auctioned Monday include Kaki for $60.00 million, Casma-Anaco for $27.58 million, Mata for $90.78 million, and Maulpa, for $61.37 million.
A total of 131 companies are competing for 20 contracts to be sold this week with the winners determined purely by the size of their bids.
